correctness.rationale: The centered compression has exact even–odd signed Gram blocks; determinant normalization is |det T|=\(H_m(0,\beta)^2/[H_m(-1/2,\beta)H_m(1/2,\beta)]\), and strict Hankel positivity removes all omitted half-eigenvalues. Jacobi monic squared norms prove the finite exact gamma formula. Digamma strict concavity proves strict beta monotonicity. Barnes G asymptotics and an expansion of symmetric gamma ratios \(u(t)=1/(4t)+O(t^{-2})\) with all \(t\ge m\) yield a uniform relative \(O(m^{-1})\) bound over \(\beta>-1\). Independently replayed exact integer-weight moment and rational Jacobi product checks plus noninteger/large-bandwidth tests corroborate but do not replace the proof; no finite experiment is claimed to establish the infinite-range conclusion.

originality.rationale: The theorem establishes a new-to-the-inspected-sources spectrum-invariant statement: an exact spectral determinant ratio for zonal hemisphere concentration with real Gegenbauer parameter, strict parameter monotonicity, and a single error estimate uniform in arbitrarily growing parameter/bandwidth. The main spherical Slepian sources formulate and numerically analyze concentration spectra; the classical Jacobi/Selberg formulas separately evaluate moment determinants, and Deift–Its–Krasovsky cover fixed-symbol Fisher–Hartwig asymptotic settings with a boundary-jump caveat. None of the materially inspected statements asserts or directly supplies the complete uniform crossover. Residual risk of an equivalent signed-Hankel specialization is explicitly recorded; a failed text search is not treated as a proof of novelty.
residual_risks: A signed Jacobi weight or Toeplitz–Hankel determinant paper might encode the exact gamma ratio under a different normalization without naming Slepian eigenvalues.
General Fisher–Hartwig methods may yield the fixed-beta asymptotic constant after a boundary-jump specialization, although no inspected theorem states the uniform beta/m crossover.
Semantic search results and inspected literature cannot prove that no unsearched historical equivalent exists.

value.rationale: The determinant |det(2C-I)| is a canonical collective half-concentration invariant for zonal spherical spectral analysis, not an arbitrarily selected coefficient. The closed law determines it at every bandwidth and continuous ultraspherical parameter, proves strict dimension-parameter monotonicity, and exposes a nontrivial dimension-to-bandwidth transition: the leading constant varies by \(2^{1/4}\) across noncommuting high-dimension and high-bandwidth limits. The uniform two-parameter theorem captures a structurally meaningful regime absent from the inspected fixed-dimensional concentration literature; it neither rests solely on numeric novelty nor claims a theorem about full higher-dimensional spherical spectra.
